jobs.title: Director, Business Intelligence & Go-to-Market
jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Summary

A member of the Market Strategy leadership team, reporting to the VP, Market Strategy, the Director, Business Intelligence & Go-to-Market is responsible for translating commercial strategy into action and using market, customer, and business data to measure performance, identify opportunities, and continuously optimize plans. The role brings together business intelligence, market analytics, strategic planning, and go-to-market capabilities to drive stronger commercial decision-making and execution. The ultimate objective is to identify and unlock growth opportunities, sharpen commercial priorities and investment, and elevate execution to deliver against Arterra’s long-term plan.

The Director will lead the development of analytics, insights, and tools that enable the business to clearly understand where to play, how to win, and where to invest, while partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and senior leadership to turn strategy into measurable results. This position is based out of our Mississauga head office (hybrid work model / 3 days in office) and reports to the Vice-President of Market Strategy.

Key Responsibilities

Business Performance Management. A key contributor to the monthly business cycle informing management on performance KPIs across category, volume, and market share (brand, geography, segment, pack etc.). Leverage compelling story-telling to clearly articulate performance drivers in a concise manner, with clear calls-to-action / next steps.
Data Transformation: lead the journey in partnership with IT to fully democratize and automate our data set. First, solidify the integrity and accuracy of our data in order to create organizational trust. Second, build visulisation tools with PowerBI that prevents the need for offline work. Finally, support the change management involved by offering training and assist first time users in the adoption journey.
Commercial Planning: Lead the development of the annual commercial planning process for the sales team on a national and regional basis. Act as an ‘entreprise’ ambassador to the commercial teams to help facilitate strategy translation into regional execution.
Go-To-Market: day to day execution of our annual sales plan through price, promotion, NPD launches, and shopper programming performance. Strive for continuous improvement in commercial ROI across the different levers of investment. Lead the monthly market PRs with clear & concise storytelling on key performance drivers.
Leadership: Raising the talent level through continuous development of a team of direct reports and their respective team members. Building strong succession planning and recruitment initiatives. Drive engagement across the team. Act as a senior leader of the market strategy group.

What You Bring

10+ years progressive experience in packaged goods industry specially sales intelligence, FP&A, RGM, GTM functions
Previous leadership experience managing mid-size teams ( Alc Bev Experience
Proven analytical and storytelling capability.
Ability to diagnose complex business problems and communicate outputs clearly through compelling visuals and excellent verbal skills.
Demonstrated ability to influence and collaborate with Senior Leadership both internally and externally
Provides direction, support, reinforcement and coaching to create a high-commitment, high-performing work team
Utilizes a disciplined approach to define problems, identify root causes, evaluate data from a variety of sources, generate alternative solutions and choose the best solution
Ability to use information in an effective and timely manner to allocate resources and achieve business goals
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Demonstrated organizational, co-ordination and time management skills
Demonstrates a high level of follow through and ability to meet multiple deadlines

What We Offer

Hybrid work model, allowing employees to balance remote and in-office work.
Competitive Salary and Bonus.
Benefits and Pension Plan.
Product Allowances.
Training & Development Programs.
Tuition Reimbursement.
Commitment to Corporate Social Responsibility.
A chance to explore and learn more about the Wine industry.

COMPENSATION
: Budgeted Range – $126,111 - $173,403. The budgeted range takes into account several factors and qualifications that are considered in making compensation decisions including experience, education, training, licenses, certifications, and other business and organizational requirements. Base pay is only one component of the total rewards offering at Arterra.

The budgeted range will align with qualifications, including experience, education, training, licenses, certifications, and other business and organizational requirements.

We are committed to establishing a qualified workforce that reflects the diverse population it serves and we encourage applications from all qualified individuals. We are also committed to preventing and removing barriers to employment for people with disabilities, and we invite you to inform us should you have any accessibility or accommodation needs.

jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
Horizon Recruitment
is recruiting for a Vice President, Finance
to join a growing organization in the real estate and hospitality sector. This is a key leadership opportunity to shape financial strategy, support major investment decisions, and drive long-term growth within a unique resort environment. Working closely with the executive team, the VP Finance will oversee financial operations, lead strategic planning, and provide the insights needed to make sound business decisions. The role also provides oversight of technology strategy, ensuring financial systems and digital tools support business goals. This opportunity is well suited to an experienced finance leader who enjoys being close to the business, values a strong sense of community, and wants to make a meaningful impact. Whether you are building on your hospitality experience or seeking a lifestyle change that better aligns your career and personal goals, this role offers the chance to contribute to a growing organization while working with a close-knit leadership team.

Responsibilities

Lead financial strategy and long-term planning to support business growth, capital investment, and financial sustainability.
Partner with senior leadership and department heads to turn financial insights into practical business decisions.
Oversee budgeting, forecasting, cash flow planning, and financial performance reporting.
Ensure accurate financial statements, strong internal controls, and compliance with accounting standards, tax requirements, and regulations.
Evaluate capital projects, expansion opportunities, and financing options to support future investment.
Identify opportunities to improve profitability, manage costs, and strengthen operational performance.
Provide strategic oversight of IT, including technology budgets, system investments, cybersecurity, and data management.
Champion improvements to financial systems, reporting tools, automation, and business intelligence.
Lead financial and operational risk management, including compliance with ISO 14001 and other relevant standards.
Manage relationships with external auditors, lenders, financial partners, and regulatory bodies.
Lead and develop the finance team, including oversight of compensation and benefits, while building a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
Work across departments to improve efficiency, support a strong safety culture, and ensure financial decisions contribute to an exceptional guest experience.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum 10 years of progressive financial leadership experience, ideally within hospitality, resorts, real estate, or a related industry.
MBA or CPA designation preferred.
Strong background in financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and risk management.
Experience evaluating capital investments, financing structures, and business growth opportunities.
Ability to interpret complex financial information and provide clear, actionable recommendations to senior leaders.
Experience overseeing financial systems and working with technology teams to improve reporting, automation, and data security.
Proven ability to lead and develop teams while working effectively across different business functions.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to engage executives, business partners, and external stakeholders.
A hands-on, practical leadership style suited to a lean organization where collaboration and accountability matter.
An appreciation for community-focused workplaces, with a commitment to safety, guest experience, integrity, teamwork, and work-life balance.

Remuneration

$160,000-$170,000 plus a generous bonus and RRSP matching program.

Only candidates eligible to work in Canada will be considered.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Lead the global capital strategy for a newly public, high-growth technology company at a pivotal stage of expansion. Bring your investor network and capital-markets expertise to drive transformational financing, strategic partnerships, and M&A opportunities. Partner directly with the Founder, Board, and Senior Executive team in a highly visible CFO role with significant influence, upside, and equity participation. Home base of either Toronto
is strongly preferred.

Who- the Company:

Swim Recruiting is conducting a confidential search on behalf of an AI and media technology company operating across Canada, the United States, and various countries in Europe.

The company delivers in an integrated solution with one connected platform. They are not selling new hardware, they are not pushing a major system change. They are taking data and intelligence that customers often already have, and strategically connecting the information to monetize real results. So far the company has over 50 clients in 4+ countries and their product is being used in thousands of locations. Following a recent reverse takeover and stock exchange listing, the organization has entered its next phase of growth: scaling their proven platform into new markets and verticals while continuing to build the capital markets profile of a public growth company.

What- the Role:

Swim Recruiting has been engaged on the search for a new Global Chief Financial Officer
whose first priority is capital markets: raising capital for a TSXV growth company and keeping the market informed and engaged once it is raised. It suits a capital markets professional who has led small-cap raises as a CFO, VP Finance, or corporate development lead and is ready to own the full mandate.

The CFO will run financings from term sheet to close, starting with private placements, bridge financing and working capital facilities, and growing into larger equity and debt rounds as the company scales. Working alongside the Founder & CEO and the Global COO, the CFO will be a primary face of the company to brokers, investors, and lenders and will play a key role in translating the growth story into funding.

This is not a back-office finance role. We are looking for an externally-facing CFO who already grown a public company and who arrives with an active network of institutional investors, private credit and structured finance providers, investment bankers, and strategic partners ready to engage with.

This is a rare opportunity to be the architect of the capital strategy for a newly public, fast-scaling technology company.

What- the Responsibilities:

Capital Markets & Fundraising
Lead brokered and non-brokered private placements, convertibles, and warrant structures from mandate through to close
Secure and manage bridge, working capital, and asset-based facilities, including LC and credit lines tied to inventory and deployment cycles
Build and work a pipeline of Canadian investment dealers, family offices, high-net-worth and institutional investors, and private lenders
Prepare the materials that win capital: investor decks, financial models, data rooms, and term sheet analysis
Run investor meetings, non-deal roadshows, and conferences in Canada and the US

Investor Relations & Disclosure
Own investor relations for a TSXV-listed company: shareholders, analysts, market makers, and IR firms
Prepare news releases, MD&A, and financing disclosure in coordination with securities counsel
Ensure every financing is structured, approved, and filed in compliance with TSXV policies and Canadian securities requirements

Capital Strategy
Build and maintain a 12 to 24 month funding roadmap that balances dilution, cost of capital, and growth speed
Advise the Founder & Chairman, Global COO, and Board on capital structure and on financing for strategic or M&A opportunities

Finance Oversight
Oversee reporting, treasury, and controls with country finance leads across Canada, the US, Europe, and Turkey, to public company standards
Present to the Board and Audit Committee on cash position, runway, and funding plans

Who- The Candidate:

10+ years in finance
, with at least 5 in Canadian capital markets as a public company CFO or VP Finance, in corporate development, or in investment banking or equity capital markets at a Canadian dealer
A track record of personally leading small-cap raises
on the TSXV, CSE, or TSX, typically C$2M to C$30M per round (we will ask about the amount, structure, and your role in each)
A current network
of Canadian investment dealers, family offices, high-net-worth investors, and private lenders you can put to work in your first 90 days. This network is a requirement of the role, not a nice-to-have.
Working knowledge of TSXV policies, NI 45-106 prospectus exemptions, continuous disclosure, and IFRS and current PIFF
CPA, CFA, or equivalent designation
Comfortable operating at both altitudes — the strategic capital-raising mandate and enough command of the underlying financials to be credible with investors, lenders, and the Board.
Experience in technology, AI/analytics, media, or adjacent sectors is highly preferred, almost required.. however we will consider CFOs with highly relevant work experience and networks who perhaps haven’t yet worked in this space.
Willingness to travel regularly across the company's markets in North America, UK, and Europe.

How Much:

The new CFO will receive a base salary commensurate with depth and breadth of work experience and relevant of investor networks, in the range of $240,000 to $300,000 Canadian
. The upside
for this role
is robust
. The CFO will be eligible for an annual bonus program and equity. The CEO/Founder will have their CFO’s total earnings increase in-step with the company’s growth. We are looking for a CFO who thrives on having “skin in the game”, and who is highly motivated by the potential rewards of their sweat equity, corporate finance savvy, and successful capital raising activities.

Where:

Home base of Greater Toronto Area, with frequent business travel across North America, as well occasional trips to the UK, Europe, and potentially Asia. Must have a valid passport and no travel restrictions.

When & How to Apply:

Swim Recruiting will be conducting initial screening and interviewing, and presenting the resumes and profiles of short-listed candidates directly to the hiring team. If you are interested in this opportunity so far and would like to hear more, please hit “ APPLY
” and a Recruitment Consultant at SWIM will reach out if there is a potential for a match. Thank you!

Job Description

Help Secure the Future of Education at Algonquin College | Join Algonquin College: A Forbes Best Employer (2026), Recognized for an Exceptional Workplace Culture and Named One of Canada's Best Employers for Diversity

There has never been a more important time to lead information security in higher education. As technology continues to transform how we teach, learn, work, and connect, the cybersecurity landscape is evolving at an unprecedented pace. Institutions face increasingly complex threats that require strong leadership, strategic foresight, and a proactive approach to risk management. At Algonquin College, we're embracing digital transformation while protecting the information, systems, and services that support our learners, employees, and communities. We are seeking an exceptional information security leader to join our team as Associate Director, Information Security
. This is more than an information security leadership role. It is an opportunity to shape enterprise strategy, influence institutional decision-making, strengthen organizational resilience, and help enable innovation through secure and trusted technology solutions. Reporting to the Chief Digital Officer, you will provide strategic leadership for the College's cybersecurity program, overseeing governance, risk management, security operations, incident response, compliance, and cybersecurity awareness while serving as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and the Board of Governors.

As our Associate Director, Information Security, you'll play a critical role in protecting the College's digital future while helping advance one of Canada's leading post-secondary institutions.

What You'll Be Doing...

Lead Enterprise Cybersecurity Strategy & Governance

Lead the College's cybersecurity strategy, governance, and risk management framework.
Advise senior leaders on cybersecurity risks, priorities, and emerging threats.
Provide cybersecurity reporting and guidance to leadership and governance bodies.

Strengthen Cybersecurity Operations & Organizational Resilience

Lead cybersecurity operations, incident response, and enterprise security services.
Strengthen organizational resilience through risk mitigation, recovery planning, and emergency response.
Embed cybersecurity practices across technology services, projects, and digital initiatives.

Advance Compliance, Risk Management & Continuous Improvement

Establish cybersecurity policies, standards, and compliance frameworks.
Lead audits, assessments, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Provide oversight of technology risk, security controls, and regulatory compliance.

Build Strategic Partnership & Serve as Trusted Advisor

Build strategic partnerships with internal and external stakeholders to advance cybersecurity objectives.
Foster a culture of cybersecurity awareness, accountability, and risk-informed decision-making.
Translate complex cybersecurity risks into actionable business recommendations and represent the College in relevant industry forums.

Required Qualifications

Education & Credentials

A minimum four-year degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business Technology Management, or a related discipline
A recognized cybersecurity or information security designation such as: Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC) Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA)

Experience

Nine (9) years of progressively responsible experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk management, or a related field
Significant experience leading enterprise-wide cybersecurity programs, initiatives, and teams
Extensive experience developing, implementing, and managing cybersecurity programs within a complex organization
Experience in cybersecurity governance, risk management, security operations, incident response, vulnerability management, and technology risk assessment
Experience advising senior leaders and governance bodies on cybersecurity risks, mitigation strategies, and investment priorities
Experience managing cybersecurity projects, operating budgets, vendor relationships, and contracted services
Experience leading security investigations, incident response activities, and recovery efforts
Experience conducting security reviews, audits, risk assessments, and compliance-related activities
Experience building collaborative partnerships across diverse stakeholder groups

Key Qualifications Include

Advanced knowledge of cybersecurity governance, risk management, security operations, incident response, and information security controls
Demonstrated expertise developing cybersecurity strategies, policies, standards, and enterprise security programs
Thorough understanding of cybersecurity frameworks, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and leading practices
Knowledge of cloud security, network security, identity and access management, security monitoring technologies, disaster recovery planning, and business continuity practices
Strong analytical and risk assessment skills with the ability to evaluate complex threats and business impacts
Proven leadership, change management, and project management capabilities
Exceptional communication and executive presentation skills
Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Strong consultation, negotiation, and relationship management skills
Experience with enterprise cybersecurity technologies, security monitoring platforms, risk management tools, and compliance reporting solutions

Ready to Help Protect and Enable the Future of Algonquin College?

If you're energized by leading cybersecurity strategy, strengthening organizational resilience, and enabling innovation through secure technology, we encourage you to apply.

Join us in helping create a safer, stronger, and more digitally secure future for our College community.

This position is paid at Payband 13
Vacancy is for P02099

with a minimum 3 days onsite
, in conjunction with the College's
Flexible Work Arrangement Policy
.

Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Accessibility (IDEA): We are proud to be the first Ontario college to implement an Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion policy, fostering an inclusive workplace where all employees feel respected and valued. Affinity Group Conversation Communities | Inclusion & Diversity & Truth and Reconciliation

Algonquin College uses artificial intelligence technology to assist in screening and assessing applicants and their applications, while ensuring that all processes respect and uphold the provisions of applicable collective agreements above all else.

Accessibility

Algonquin College values diversity and is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and culturally respectful workplace. We offer an inclusive work environment and encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, including Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, members of racialized groups, and individuals from diverse communities. If you require accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact the Human Resources department at humanresources@algonquincollege.com. A recognized cybersecurity or information security designation such as: Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC) Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA)

Experience

Nine (9) years of progressively responsible experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk management, or a related field
Significant experience leading enterprise-wide cybersecurity programs, initiatives, and teams
Extensive experience developing, implementing, and managing cybersecurity programs within a complex organization
Experience in cybersecurity governance, risk management, security operations, incident response, vulnerability management, and technology risk assessment
Experience advising senior leaders and governance bodies on cybersecurity risks, mitigation strategies, and investment priorities
Experience managing cybersecurity projects, operating budgets, vendor relationships, and contracted services
Experience leading security investigations, incident response activities, and recovery efforts
Experience conducting security reviews, audits, risk assessments, and compliance-related activities
Experience building collaborative partnerships across diverse stakeholder groups

Key Qualifications Include

Advanced knowledge of cybersecurity governance, risk management, security operations, incident response, and information security controls
Demonstrated expertise developing cybersecurity strategies, policies, standards, and enterprise security programs
Thorough understanding of cybersecurity frameworks, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and leading practices
Knowledge of cloud security, network security, identity and access management, security monitoring technologies, disaster recovery planning, and business continuity practices
Strong analytical and risk assessment skills with the ability to evaluate complex threats and business impacts
Proven leadership, change management, and project management capabilities
Exceptional communication and executive presentation skills
Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Strong consultation, negotiation, and relationship management skills
Experience with enterprise cybersecurity technologies, security monitoring platforms, risk management tools, and compliance reporting solutions
